data.name: Singapore
data.summary: Singapore has no capital gains tax on investment gains, no tax on Singapore one-tier dividends, does not tax foreign-sourced investment income received by individuals (dividends, interest, gains), has had no estate duty since 15 February 2008, and has no gift or wealth tax. The main costs for a wealthy family are high stamp duties on buying residential property as foreigners (additional buyer's stamp duty, ABSD, of up to 65% depending on buyer status and number of properties), progressive property tax on homes, and the high cost of living. Residence for a non-citizen investor normally runs through the EDB Global Investor Programme (PR) or an employment pass via a family office.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Territorial personal income tax (0-24%) on Singapore-source income; foreign-sourced investment income received by individuals is exempt.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if ordinarily residing in Singapore or present/working 183 days or more in the prior calendar year; needs an immigration status (PR via GIP, employment pass, dependant pass).

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax. IRAS states gains from the sale of property, shares and financial instruments are generally not taxable for individuals. Only gains that amount to trading (badges of trade) are taxed as income at progressive rates up to 24%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No tax on capital gains of any amount; no holding period required.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains are taxable as income if IRAS treats the activity as a trade (frequency, intention, financing, holding period). Seller's stamp duty (SSD) of up to 16% applies to residential property sold within the SSD holding period (rate up to 16% for properties bought from 4 July 2025, per PwC; the length of the holding period was not verified from an opened source). Section 10L (foreign disposal gains of entities without economic substance, from 2024) applies to entities, not to individuals holding directly.

sources.title: Gains from sale of property, shares and financial instruments

capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax for a private investor holding for investment. Local real estate 0% assumes a sale after the seller's stamp duty holding period; inside it SSD of up to 16% of price applies.
capital_gains.professional_trader: If IRAS concludes an individual is trading (frequent short-term dealing, intention to profit from resale, borrowed money), gains become income taxed at resident rates up to 24% (above SGD 1,000,000). Long-term portfolio investment is ordinarily capital.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities. SSD on residential property sold within the SSD holding period.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Gains on foreign assets are not taxed; foreign-sourced income received by individuals is exempt (except through a Singapore partnership).

dividends.summary: Dividends from Singapore companies are exempt under the one-tier system. Foreign dividends received by individuals (other than through a Singapore partnership) are not taxable, so foreign source withholding tax is the final cost and is not credited.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: All one-tier dividends exempt; foreign-sourced investment income exempt for individuals.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign income received through a Singapore partnership is taxable. Singapore has no comprehensive income tax treaty with the United States, so US-source dividends paid to a Singapore-resident non-US person bear the 30% US statutory withholding tax.
dividends.rate_basis: One-tier dividends are exempt in shareholders' hands; foreign-sourced dividends received by a resident individual are exempt, so the Singapore rate is 0% and only source-country withholding remains.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Singapore levies no withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (0% under domestic law and all treaties).
dividends.treaty_network: Large network (PwC lists about 98 partners), but the treaties with the United States, Hong Kong, Chile and Bermuda are limited (shipping/air transport or information exchange only). US dividends therefore bear 30% US WHT for a Singapore resident, a real cost for a US-heavy portfolio.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Singapore companies pay 17% CIT; a family office fund vehicle can obtain exemptions under sections 13O/13U (MAS-approved) for specified investment income.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual property tax on the property's annual value: owner-occupied residential 0% to 32% (progressive), non-owner-occupied residential 12% to 36%, non-residential 10%. Buying residential property: BSD up to 6% plus ABSD up to 65% depending on residency status and number of properties (highest for foreigners and entities); nationals of certain FTA countries are treated like Singapore citizens.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax: estate duty was removed for deaths on and after 15 February 2008. No gift tax. Transfers of Singapore shares or property to children can attract stamp duty, and a gift of residential property attracts buyer's stamp duty (and ABSD) on market value.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: No tax of any amount on inheritances or gifts to children.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Stamp duty applies to transfers of Singapore real estate (BSD/ABSD on market value) and to transfers of Singapore shares by instrument; the share stamp duty rate was not verified. Income of the estate after death remains subject to income tax.
inheritance.gift_tax: None. Stamp duty applies to gifts of Singapore shares and real estate.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on foreign assets either.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Not applicable; there is no estate duty for any decedent dying on or after 15 February 2008.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual ordinarily resides in Singapore (apart from reasonable temporary absences) or is physically present or works in Singapore for 183 days or more in the calendar year before the year of assessment. Foreigners staying over three consecutive calendar years are treated as resident for all three years by concession.

routes.name: Global Investor Programme (permanent residence) - Option A, business
routes.requirements: Invest at least SGD 10 million in a new or existing Singapore business, with a substantial business track record. Grants PR to the investor and immediate family. Thresholds per a 2026 professional summary of EDB's May 2025 factsheet; confirm with EDB.

routes.name: Global Investor Programme - Option C, single family office
routes.requirements: Set up a Singapore single family office with at least SGD 200 million AUM and deploy at least SGD 50 million into specified Singapore investment categories; PR for the principal and immediate family. Option B (SGD 25 million into a GIP-select fund) also exists.

routes.name: Employment pass via own family office (13O/13U fund manager)
routes.requirements: Family members employed as investment professionals by a single family office can hold employment passes; dependants' passes for spouse and children. Requirements are set by MOM/MAS and were not verified in detail.

corporate.summary: 17% flat CIT with partial exemption on the first SGD 200,000 of chargeable income; one-tier system (no tax on dividends paid out, no dividend WHT). For YA2026 a 50% CIT rebate (capped at SGD 40,000, or SGD 38,000 plus a SGD 2,000 grant) applies. Pillar Two: Multinational Enterprise (Minimum Tax) Act 2024 introduces the domestic top-up tax (DTT) and MTT from financial years starting 1 January 2025; UTPR not adopted.
corporate.special_zones: Fund tax incentives under sections 13O (onshore fund) and 13U (enhanced-tier fund) exempt specified income of family office vehicles, subject to MAS approval, minimum AUM, local spending and investment professionals.

housekeeper_monthly.description: Live-in migrant domestic worker employed by a foreign (non-citizen) family: MOM monthly levy SGD 300 for the first helper (2026 rate; the SGD 60 concession needs a Singapore-citizen child under 16, or a citizen/qualifying PR aged 67+ or with a disability, so it does not apply to a foreign family; a second helper costs SGD 450) plus salary SGD 620, MOM's latest published average monthly salary of a new helper hired from overseas (September 2021; transfer helpers about SGD 40 more). Singapore has no statutory minimum wage for domestic workers. Excludes food, lodging, mandatory insurance and agency fees; experienced helpers in 2026 are often paid more, so treat as a floor.

Cross-check: URA's 'Rentals of Non-Landed Residential Buildings, Quarterly' dataset on data.gov.sg (d_149ac00a2734bb0a03867bbe2ec0e7b0, 2026-Q2) gives a median of project medians of 5.76 across 154 projects (3,063 contracts) in postal districts 9, 10 and 11 (D9 5.94, D10 5.58, D11 5.19; 75th percentile of projects 6.72); the dataset metadata does not state the unit; read as SGD per sq ft per month (the unit agencies use for URA rents, e.g. Knight Frank's Q1 2026 update charts URA Realis rents in S$ per sq ft per month), it would give roughly SGD 15,500 for 2,690 sq ft, the same order as the Savills figure. Not used for the score because the unit is not confirmed in the dataset. The URA figures cover all unit sizes, and smaller units rent at higher psf. Housekeeper salary source: MOM written answer to PQ, 3 Nov 2021 (https://www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/parliament-questions-and-replies/2021/1103-written-answer-to-pq-on-data-on-employer-types-and-market-salaries-for-the-existing-mdws). Purchase prices and family health insurance were not sourced. Foreign buyers face high ABSD on residential purchases (up to 65% depending on status), so most foreign families rent until they obtain PR.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens stay taxed by the US on worldwide income and estates. Singapore has no comprehensive income tax treaty with the US; since Singapore does not tax foreign investment income, the US layer is the full cost. Singapore company or fund structures may be CFCs/PFICs for a US person.
open_questions: GIP thresholds (SGD 10m / 25m / 200m AUM with SGD 50m deployment) are from a professional summary of EDB's 2025 factsheet; EDB's own page did not show the figures.

Purchase price per m2 and family private health insurance not sourced. Prime rent is the median of 14 asking rents for 4-bedroom Bukit Timah/Holland condos on EdgeProp; helper salary is MOM's 2021 average (no newer official figure found).

income.name: Singapore

income_tax.summary: Residents pay progressive tax from 0% to 24% (YA2026 schedule, income of 2025); non-residents pay 24% on most income or the higher of 15% and resident rates on employment. Foreign-sourced income received in Singapore by individuals is generally exempt. Foreign nationals cannot contribute to CPF, so there is no social security cost.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Foreign nationals and their employers are precluded from CPF; permanent residents contribute at reduced rates for two years (20% employee rate for citizens and PRs after year three, OW ceiling SGD 8,000 a month). Medisave for self-employed not covered on the opened pages, but applies to citizens and PRs. Personal allowance shown is earned income relief (lesser of actual or SGD 1,000, under 55); total reliefs are capped at SGD 80,000.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. The brackets are on chargeable income for YA2026 (income earned in 2025); the tax year 2026 schedule (YA2027) was not separately verified.

sources.title: Singapore - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: YA2027 (income of 2026) schedule: PwC's page shows YA2024 onwards rates and mentions no YA2027 change; the IRAS rates page was truncated.
Self-employed Medisave not relevant to foreigners; not verified.

regimes.name: Employment Pass (EP)
regimes.description: Work pass for foreign professionals; not a tax regime. The minimum qualifying salary is SGD 5,600 a month at age 23 and under, rising to SGD 10,700 at 45+ (financial services SGD 6,200-11,800), and applications must also earn 40 COMPASS points unless the fixed salary is at least SGD 22,500 a month. For new applications from 1 January 2027 the minimum becomes SGD 6,000-11,500 (financial services SGD 6,600-12,700). Tax is standard; foreign income received in Singapore is generally exempt for individuals, but pay for work done in Singapore is Singapore-sourced.
regimes.duration_note: Passes are renewable; validity length not stated on the opened page. Minimum shown is the entry level (SGD 5,600 x 12), age-dependent.
open_questions: General EP validity and renewal terms are not on the MOM eligibility page (only that certain tech occupations can get 5 years).

regimes.name: Overseas Networks and Expertise (ONE) Pass
regimes.description: Five-year personalised pass for top talent: a fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 30,000 (SGD 22,500 on the AI and Tech track from 28 January 2027) from one employer, with an established overseas or Singapore company (market cap USD 500 million or revenue USD 200 million). Holders can start, operate and work for multiple companies. It does not change tax: pay for work done in Singapore is taxed at the normal resident rates, and as a foreigner the holder has no CPF.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 5 years for first-time holders, renewable for 5 years each time (10 shown as first term plus one renewal).

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: there is no digital nomad visa; remote workers cannot use a tourist stay to work. Skilled employees need an Employment Pass (SGD 5,600+ a month and COMPASS points, or SGD 22,500+ a month exempt from COMPASS). The Overseas Networks and Expertise (ONE) Pass for high earners was not verified on an opened page.

succession.name: Singapore
succession.summary: Singapore has no forced heirship: non-Muslims may leave their estate freely, with family members able to apply for provision. Muslims follow Islamic shares and can will one third. Trusts are well developed and Hague-style recognition is in the Recognition of Trusts Act, but the Convention itself is not in force and there is no foundation law.
succession.family_claims: Spouse, children and certain dependants may apply for provision under the Inheritance (Family Provision) Act 1966. Muslims: Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966, fixed shares and a one-third will limit.
succession.foreign_law_note: Common-law conflict rules: movables follow the law of domicile at death, immovables follow the law of their location. A foreigner domiciled abroad keeps foreign law for movables. A foreigner domiciled in Singapore is under Singapore law. Estate duty has been abolished since 15 February 2008.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table, but the Recognition of Trusts Act 2004 recognises trusts governed by foreign law on Hague terms. Trusts are under the Trustees Act 1967 and the Trust Companies Act 2005. Singapore has no foundation statute; families use trusts, companies limited by guarantee and the variable capital company.
open_questions: Statute names were taken from the Rajah & Tann chapter and knowledge; confirm the current Act titles on Singapore Statutes Online.
Confirm no private foundation legislation is pending.

immigration.name: Singapore
immigration.summary: EU, US and other passports are treated alike. Singapore has no passive-income, retirement or digital-nomad residence. Wealthy investors can buy permanent residence through the Global Investor Programme (from SGD 10 million into a business, SGD 25 million into a select fund, or a family office of SGD 200 million with SGD 50 million deployed locally). Everyone else needs a work pass: the Employment Pass (from about SGD 5,600 a month), the ONE Pass (SGD 30,000 a month) or the EntrePass for start-up founders.
immigration.naturalisation: Citizenship needs at least 2 years as a permanent resident and age 21 (ICA); in practice ICA weighs family ties, economic contribution and commitment, and applicants aged 16-60 must complete the Singapore Citizenship Journey. Approval is discretionary and often takes longer.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: ICA's citizenship undertaking states dual citizenship is not allowed; new citizens must renounce other nationalities.

routes.name: Global Investor Programme - Option A (business investment)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for investing at least SGD 10 million in a new or expanded Singapore business, for already very large business owners.
routes.requirements: Applicant must be one of: established business owner (3+ years' track record, company turnover of at least SGD 200 million a year), next-generation owner (turnover SGD 500 million), founder of a fast-growth company (valuation SGD 500 million, VC/PE-backed) or family-office principal (net investible assets of SGD 200 million). Interview with EDB and due diligence. Approval-in-principle is valid 6 months; investment must be made in that window; PR must be formalised within 12 months of final approval. Re-entry permit valid 5 years, renewed if the investment and business conditions are kept. Spouse and unmarried children under 21 are included; sons gain National Service liability. Option A: at least SGD 10 million in a new or existing Singapore business in an approved industry (Annex B), 30%+ shareholding and a management role, 5-year business plan with local jobs. Renewal requires continued business activity (EDB's 2023 announcement cites a headcount expectation; current figures in the factsheet section 7 were not extracted).
routes.fees_note: Fee not in the EDB factsheet; third-party sources cite SGD 20,000 (not verified).
routes.physical_presence: Re-entry permit kept alive by meeting renewal criteria; no fixed day count in the factsheet
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 as dependants. Parents and children 21+ can get a Long Term Visit Pass tied to the re-entry permit.
routes.tax_note: PR does not itself set tax residence; Singapore taxes residents on Singapore-source income and does not tax most foreign-sourced income received by individuals.

routes.name: Global Investor Programme - Option B (GIP-select fund)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for putting SGD 25 million into an EDB-approved fund that invests in Singapore companies.
routes.requirements: Applicant must be one of: established business owner (3+ years' track record, company turnover of at least SGD 200 million a year), next-generation owner (turnover SGD 500 million), founder of a fast-growth company (valuation SGD 500 million, VC/PE-backed) or family-office principal (net investible assets of SGD 200 million). Interview with EDB and due diligence. Approval-in-principle is valid 6 months; investment must be made in that window; PR must be formalised within 12 months of final approval. Re-entry permit valid 5 years, renewed if the investment and business conditions are kept. Spouse and unmarried children under 21 are included; sons gain National Service liability. Option B: SGD 25 million invested in a GIP-select fund from the applicant's own Singapore bank account; the investment must be maintained for the re-entry permit renewal.
routes.fees_note: Application fee not in the EDB factsheet.
routes.physical_presence: Re-entry permit kept alive by meeting renewal criteria; no fixed day count in the factsheet
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 as dependants. Parents and children 21+ can get a Long Term Visit Pass tied to the re-entry permit.
routes.tax_note: PR does not itself set tax residence.

routes.name: Global Investor Programme - Option C (single family office)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for setting up a Singapore single family office with SGD 200 million of assets, SGD 50 million of it deployed in Singapore.
routes.requirements: Applicant must be one of: established business owner (3+ years' track record, company turnover of at least SGD 200 million a year), next-generation owner (turnover SGD 500 million), founder of a fast-growth company (valuation SGD 500 million, VC/PE-backed) or family-office principal (net investible assets of SGD 200 million). Interview with EDB and due diligence. Approval-in-principle is valid 6 months; investment must be made in that window; PR must be formalised within 12 months of final approval. Re-entry permit valid 5 years, renewed if the investment and business conditions are kept. Spouse and unmarried children under 21 are included; sons gain National Service liability. Option C: single family office in Singapore with at least SGD 200 million AUM; at least SGD 50 million transferred to Singapore and, within 12 months of final approval, deployed in EDB-specified investments (e.g. Singapore-listed equities) and kept there for the re-entry permit's life. Applicant needs 5+ years' investment track record and SGD 200 million net investible assets.
routes.investment_options: Minimum SGD 200 million AUM in the family office; SGD 50 million of it must be in Singapore in EDB-specified investments.
routes.fees_note: Application fee not in the EDB factsheet.
routes.physical_presence: Re-entry permit kept alive by meeting renewal criteria; no fixed day count in the factsheet
routes.family: Spouse and unmarried children under 21 as dependants. Parents and children 21+ can get a Long Term Visit Pass tied to the re-entry permit.
routes.tax_note: PR does not itself set tax residence; the family office may use Singapore's 13O/13U fund tax incentives separately.

routes.name: Employment Pass (EP) including COMPASS
routes.summary: Work pass for professionals, managers and executives with a Singapore job offer at or above a minimum salary and enough points on the COMPASS test.
routes.requirements: Fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 5,600 (SGD 6,200 in financial services) for age 23 rising to SGD 10,700 (SGD 11,800) at 45+, for applications before 1 January 2027; SGD 6,000 (SGD 6,600) rising to SGD 11,500 (SGD 12,700) from 1 January 2027 for new applications and 1 January 2028 for renewals. Must also score 40 points on COMPASS unless exempt (e.g. salary of SGD 22,500 a month or more, intra-company transferee).
routes.fees_note: Application and issuance fees not on the MOM pages fetched.
routes.physical_presence: Live and work in Singapore; pass lapses if employment ends
routes.processing_time: Not stated on fetched pages. Validity: up to 2 years first, up to 3 on renewal (5 for certain tech skills).
routes.family: Eligible family members can get Dependant's Passes or Long Term Visit Passes (separate MOM criteria).

routes.name: Overseas Networks & Expertise (ONE) Pass
routes.summary: Five-year pass letting top earners or achievers work for several Singapore companies or run their own, with no employer tie.
routes.requirements: Fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 30,000 for the 12 months before applying (or from a Singapore employer), from one employer; or annual income from other sources above SGD 360,000 per MOM FAQ; or outstanding achievements in listed sectors. A new AI and Tech track opens 28 January 2027. No levy or quota; exempt from COMPASS.
routes.fees_note: Fees not on the MOM pages fetched.
routes.family: Passes for eligible family members; spouse may apply to work on a Letter of Consent.
routes.tax_note: Working in Singapore may make you liable to income tax.

routes.name: EntrePass
routes.summary: Pass for founders of a venture-backed or innovative-technology start-up registered in Singapore.
routes.requirements: Hold at least 30% of an ACRA-registered private limited company that is venture-backed or owns innovative technology, and meet one criterion: raised at least SGD 100,000 in a single funding round, supported by a recognised incubator or accelerator, or founded and sold a tech business. Excluded businesses include food courts, bars, massage and TCM. The old SGD 50,000 paid-up capital rule was removed in 2017.
routes.fees_note: Fees not on the MOM pages fetched.
routes.physical_presence: Operate the business in Singapore; renewal tested on business performance
routes.processing_time: Validity: up to 1 year for new pass and first renewal, up to 2 years after (per MOM search snippet).
routes.family: Passes for eligible family members (MOM 'Passes for family' page, not read).
